clue.text: Unable to tip' the same government again?

definitions.meaning: having no coins in your pocket leaves you unable to give a tip
an election that leaves the ruling party in place means things stay as they were

explanation.definitionFit: Having no loose coins means you cannot tip, and an unaltered government means things are unaltered.

clue.text: Too busy to 'get round in Northern Ireland with me?

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the abbreviation for the province
get round asks the little word to turn about and face the other way

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are too busy to buy a round in Belfast with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get round' turns TO into OT, and 'in' puts that inside NI to make NOTI; ME follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no spare hours is the idiom for being fully occupied.

clue.text: Left in a certain situation to drive home the argument

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for left is placed within the situation word

parts.note: a cinch is something that is a dead certainty

explanation.surface: Someone stranded in a sure thing uses it to win a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a deal or dispute decisively is to seal it, which is what driving home an argument does.

clue.text: Calms down a wild beast

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters are running loose and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A tamer soothes a ferocious animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm that subsides or lessens in force is said to die away, which is calming down.

clue.text: Huge bird without which few ports could function

definitions.meaning: a very large wading bird of the long-legged, long-necked kind

definitions.text: without which few ports could function
definitions.meaning: the tall lifting machine that loads and unloads cargo ships at docks

explanation.definitionFit: A crane is both a bird and a lifting machine, and a giant one is huge either way.

clue.text: He goes after a postcard about a Red Indian tribesman

indicators.note: goes after puts the pronoun at the end of the rest
about tells us the abbreviation goes round the second letter a

parts.note: PC is the usual abbreviation for postcard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man sends a postcard about a Native American warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the second A inside PC to give PAC; 'goes after' puts HE after A + PAC. 'Red Indian' is a dated term for a Native American.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a Native American people of the south-western United States, so one of them is a member of that tribe.

clue.text: Child's domain from Kanga's instructions to Milne initially

parts.note: Kanga, the mother kangaroo in A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh, would tell her baby Roo to go and play

indicators.note: initially signals that only the opening letter of the author's name is used

explanation.surface: A children's book character gives orders to her author about a nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: Kanga's instruction to her baby is 'Play, Roo!', and 'initially' takes M from Milne.
explanation.definitionFit: A room set aside for children's games and toys is a youngster's territory.

clue.text: Outstanding feature on a fellow bowled by a left-hander.

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature that sticks out, so it stands out literally
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A protruding face on a man who was bowled out by a left-handed cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a chinaman is the delivery a left-arm wrist-spinner bowls, turning into a right-handed batsman. 'Outstanding' means sticking out, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated cricket term for a left-arm unorthodox spin delivery, the ball such a bowler sends down.

clue.text: Kind of wind flower seen -in a cathedral city

indicators.note: seen in means the flower is placed within the name of the city

parts.note: Ely is a small English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A blossom spotted in a cathedral town hints at the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze described by the compass direction it blows from, here from the sunrise side.

clue.text: A vessel that contains three bodies

definitions.text: A vessel that contains three bodies

parts.words: A vessel that contains three bodies
parts.note: the bodies are not corpses but hulls: a boat built with three of them side by side

explanation.surface: A ship carrying three dead people.
explanation.definitionFit: A multihull sailing boat with a main hull and two outriggers, each hull a body.

clue.text: Customs a sailor strikes about

indicators.note: about means the word for strikes goes around the sailor

parts.note: hits are strikes or blows
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the crossword sailor

explanation.surface: Customs officers watch a sailor lashing out.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular practices or usual ways of behaving are routines.

clue.text: Gay philanderer who broke the Highway Code?

definitions.meaning: the womanising captain in John Gay's 1728 ballad opera The Beggar's Opera
a highwayman breaks the law of the highway; the Highway Code is Britain's book of road rules

explanation.definitionFit: Captain Macheath is the highwayman hero of John Gay's Beggar's Opera, a robber with many lovers.

clue.text: The country, we hear, could be on the slippery slope!

definitions.text: could be on the slippery slope

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is only spoken, so a same-sounding spelling is wanted

parts.note: Greece is the country in south-eastern Europe

explanation.surface: A nation is said to be heading for ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' tells you GREECE is said aloud and spelt GREASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lubricating fat or oil is what you would find on a slick surface.

clue.text: Charming female after spare fitment for a bedroom' light, maybe

indicators.note: fitment is read as the letters being fitted together in a new order

parts.note: a witch casts charms, so she is a female who charms

explanation.surface: An attractive woman comes after a spare fitting for a bedroom lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fitment' rearranges SPARE into PEARS, and 'after' puts WITCH after it. A pear switch is a pear-shaped switch on a cord, often by a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch shaped like the fruit, hanging from a flex, used to turn a bedside lamp on and off.

clue.text: A fight nobody pays to see?

definitions.meaning: a brawl in which everyone joins in
a show with no charge for anyone

explanation.definitionFit: A brawl open to everyone, and an event costing nobody anything.

clue.text: Northbound travellers about to call a spaniel

indicators.note: about means the turned word goes around the word for telephone
in a down clue northbound means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: reps are commercial travellers, sales representatives
to ring someone is to call them

explanation.surface: Travellers heading north are about to call a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northbound' turns REPS into SPER, and 'about' puts RING inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The springer is a breed of gundog used to flush game.

clue.text: They're simply folk who must have solid ground to work on

definitions.text: They're simply folk who must have solid ground to work on

parts.words: They're simply folk who must have solid ground to work on
parts.note: simple country people who farm the land, so earth beneath them is their workplace

explanation.definitionFit: Poor smallholders and farm labourers work the soil, and are humble country people.

clue.text: Special crusades for vehicles that have seen better days

definitions.text: vehicles that have seen better days

indicators.note: special is used to mean the letters are made up into something different

explanation.surface: Particular holy wars are compared with old bangers.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand motors have already been driven, so they are past their prime.

clue.text: Food store holding jumble sale that's not to be taken seriously

indicators.note: holding means the food store contains the jumbled letters

parts.note: a pantry is a small room for storing food

indicators.note: jumble tells us the four letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A larder hosting a jumble sale is not a serious matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumble' rearranges SALE into LEAS, and 'holding' puts that inside PANTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, joking remark is meant in fun, so it should not be taken seriously.

clue.text: A record turnover clear of deductions for a space traveller

indicators.note: turnover means the pieces before it are turned the other way

parts.note: LP, long-playing, is a record
a net sum is what remains after deductions

explanation.surface: A record company's profits after tax are discussed by an astronaut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' turns A + LP into PLA; NET follows. 'turnover' looks like business income.
explanation.definitionFit: A world orbiting the Sun wanders through space; the Greek root means wanderer.

clue.text: I'm so upset when mother grasps so sensitive a plant

indicators.note: grasps means the word for mother holds the rearranged letters

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: upset tells us the letters of the two words are overturned and mixed

explanation.surface: Someone is upset when their mother holds on to them, being so touchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges I'M SO into IMOS, and 'grasps' puts that inside MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa pudica is the plant called the sensitive plant, its leaves folding when touched.

clue.text: Wasn't against bringing in old sappers?

indicators.note: bringing in means the word for old takes the sappers inside it

parts.note: aged means old
RE, Royal Engineers, are the British Army's sappers

explanation.surface: Someone didn't object to bringing in elderly army engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To have concurred is to have not opposed something.

clue.text: Esoteric time-serving?

definitions.meaning: known only to a select few, as with private information
serving time in prison, so behind bars

explanation.definitionFit: Insider knowledge is private to a few, and a convict serving a sentence is in jail.

clue.text: Expanding trapeze about 45 inches long

indicators.note: about means the word for trapeze goes around the measure

parts.note: a trapeze is a kind of swing
an ell is an old cloth measure of 45 inches

explanation.surface: A trapeze stretches to nearly four feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The ELL is an old English unit for measuring cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing larger in size, as a bruise does, is getting bigger.

clue.text: FBI agent restraining a French gangster

indicators.note: restraining means the agent holds the French word inside

parts.note: a G-man is an American federal agent
un is French for a

explanation.surface: A federal agent arrests a French gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: An armed criminal or hoodlum, the hired gun of a gang.

clue.text: Phaetons converted into another type of carriage

indicators.note: converted tells us the letters are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: Open carriages are rebuilt as a different model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges PHAETONS; a phaeton is itself a light carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a light open horse-drawn gig named after the clergyman who first had one built.

clue.text: Is getting in support to carry on the fight

indicators.note: getting in means the little word is put inside the support

parts.note: a rest is a support, as for a cue or an arm
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gets support so they can keep battling.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose or withstand an attack is to keep battling against it.

clue.text: Terrain for the ponies Stendhal sorted out

indicators.note: sorted out tells us the author's letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: The French novelist Stendhal tidies up some pony country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' rearranges STENDHAL. The Shetland Isles lie north of Scotland and give their name to the small hardy ponies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish islands are the homeland of the small breed of pony named after them.
